question: Septal perforation and saddle-nose deformity in nasal leprosy result from granulomatous destruction of the anterior nasal cartilage and septum, and the primary treatment is multi-drug therapy (MDT) to arrest disease progression.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Nasal leprosy destroys the anterior nasal cartilage through granulomatous inflammation, causing septal perforation and saddle-nose. MDT arrests the underlying infection and is the essential first-line treatment before any consideration of surgical reconstruction.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Mycobacterium leprae preferentially involves the anterior nasal septum and inferior turbinates, causing granulomatous infiltration, then cartilage destruction, septal perforation, and ultimately saddle-nose deformity. MDT (rifampicin, dapsone, clofazimine for multibacillary leprosy) is the disease-modifying treatment. Surgical reconstruction of the saddle-nose is a later, elective procedure performed only after disease has been arrested with MDT.
